## Overview

This is a starter Quarto report. A `.qmd` file is markdown with executable
Python chunks — rendering runs the code and embeds its output, so the numbers
and figures below are regenerated from source every time.

Render it with:

```bash
just render-one report          # HTML
just render-one-pdf report      # PDF (needs TinyTeX)
```

## Setup

```{python}
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import polars as pl

from combocizes.core import summarize
```

## Data

```{python}
frame = pl.DataFrame(
    {
        "group": ["a", "a", "b", "b", "c"],
        "value": [1.0, 3.0, 10.0, 12.0, 7.0],
    }
)
frame
```

## Results

Chunk options control what appears. `echo: false` in `_quarto.yaml` hides code
globally; `#| echo: true` on a chunk overrides it.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Value aggregated by group."
result = summarize(frame, group_by="group", value="value")
result
```

@tbl-summary shows the group totals. Cross-references work off the `label`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-totals
#| fig-cap: "Total value by group."
fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(result["group"], result["total"], color="#4C72B0")
ax.set_xlabel("Group")
ax.set_ylabel("Total value")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
plt.show()
```

Inline values interpolate too: the largest group total is
`{python} f"{result['total'].max():,.1f}"`.

## Notes

- Math renders with LaTeX: $\sigma^2 = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i (x_i - \bar{x})^2$
- Import from `combocizes` directly — the package is installed in editable mode
  by `uv sync`, so edits to `src/` are picked up without reinstalling.
